blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Sunday said 638 transport network vehicle service (TNVS) partners would be granted regularized status, having already been issued provisional authority. According to the LTFRB, it had received 9,036 applications from TNVS partners with “tempo” status, a practice in which transport network companies (TNCs) onboard TNVS units on their digital platforms without securing the necessary authorizations from the agency. The application period for regularizing TNVS partners with tempo status began on Oct. 8 and will last for 30 calendar days. LTFRB Chair Greg Pua urged those affected to apply for […]...
